findings.reason: the node's own gate would fail against a correct implementation of the text as written, sending it to hunt a defect in the wrong mechanism (disposition reading) instead of the identity resolution the plan never names.
findings.text: §54 excludes `claim_disposition` for non-overlapping pointers, but `_pointer_scope_entries` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:230`) resolves each pointer's repository through `claim_repository` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1415`) -> `repository_identity` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1390`), which runs `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` in that pointer's worktree and is memoised nowhere, so the read still costs one `git` subprocess per disjoint pointer and its done-when bullet "runs `git` only in the overlapping run's worktree" is unreachable at head

findings.reason: the plan must say the counter wraps the index build's parse only, or the node implements the natural counter, sees counts it cannot reconcile with a correct incremental index, and has no stated reading to fall back on.
findings.text: §55 counts "record parses with a wrapper" and asserts "parses exactly 1" after an add and "parses none" for a fresh process, while the same section states the selected record "is still read again from disk"; the lookup path reads and parses that record and merges its staging and committed copies (`_record_with_merged_answers`, `_staging_copies_of_record`, `_committed_record_at` at `reckon/crew/review_records.py:488-505`), so a counter wrapping the parse the lookup performs counts at least one per lookup whatever the index does
